title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
one_line_claim: Nucleus Sampling prevents text degeneration (repetition, incoherence) by sampling from the dynamic nucleus of the probability distribution rather than maximizing likelihood or using fixed-size truncation.
method_summary: Nucleus Sampling dynamically selects the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds a threshold p, then samples uniformly from this adaptively-sized nucleus. The method contrasts with fixed top-k and maximization-based decoding by letting the candidate set adjust based on the model's confidence distribution at each step.

key_findings.finding: Beam search and maximization-based decoding cause degenerate repetition despite high likelihood, while Nucleus Sampling avoids both repetition and incoherence.
key_findings.quote: Even with our relatively fine-grained parameter sweep, Nucleus Sampling obtains closest perplexity to human text, as shown in Table 1.

key_findings.finding: Natural language text does not maximize probability; highest-probability sequences correspond to repetitive or incoherent output.
key_findings.quote: Natural language rarely remains in a high probability zone for multiple consecutive time steps, instead veering into lower-probability but more informative tokens.

key_findings.finding: The probability of a repeated phrase increases with each repetition, creating a positive feedback loop locking the model into degeneration.
key_findings.quote: The probability of a repeated phrase increases with each repetition, creating a positive feedback loop. We found this effect to hold for the vast majority of phrases we tested.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both identify failure modes during generation (repetition/incoherence vs. compression-induced looping/non-termination), both emphasize per-token distributional properties as signals.
differs_on: Nucleus Sampling is a decoding strategy that modulates token selection; HERALD is a predictive hazard detector that forecasts failure from logit time series.
Nucleus Sampling prevents repetition by dynamic nucleus truncation; HERALD predicts looping caused by KV-cache compression, a different mechanism.
Nucleus Sampling operates on the output probability distribution; HERALD operates on internal logit signals and is generation-strategy-agnostic.
